notes:
## New: filter voices by language

- Pick a **Language** above the voice list in the text to speech settings.
- It starts on English. Choose **All languages** to see every voice.
- It narrows the Piper voices you can download too.
- Favourites and your chosen voice always show.

## Changed: sending a QC review back

- Save the QC package with `Ctrl/Cmd+S` and send that file back to the writer.
- **Export → Return package** is gone. With a QC package open in QC, there's no Export menu.
- Check spelling and grammar with `Alt+Shift+K`.
- The file you send back keeps any review key. Writers: delete the key when the review is done.

## Changed: clicking a block

- Clicking a block in the list opens it and leaves the playhead where it is.
- `Esc` or `Enter` closes the block and moves the playhead to it.
- This works with Replay on or off.
- Record mode and locked QC packages still jump on the click.

## New: Extended AD

- The video pauses while a block is read, then carries on.
- Click **Extended** in a block, or turn it on for the whole project in the text to speech settings.
- QC reviewers hear the pauses too.

## New: Extended AD in exports

- The description track, full mix and scripts follow the pauses.
- **Export → Extended video** saves a new video that holds the picture during each pause. It needs ffmpeg.
- Turn off **Include the narration** for the programme's sound alone, to mix in a DAW.
- **Export → Pause list** saves where the video stops, as a CSV.
- To keep the video's timing, turn off **Keep the pauses**.

## New: Extended AD in Record mode

- Narrators read extended blocks with the video stopped, with no time limit.
- The Narration WAV follows the pauses, and a pause list comes with it.

## New: Amazon Polly voices

- Use Amazon's voices with your own AWS key.
- New AWS accounts can use Polly in their home region.

## New: lead-in

- Hear the moments before a block when you go back to it.
- Set **Lead-in** in Settings, under General, from 0 to 30 seconds.
- It works with Replay, `Shift+Space`, `L` and `V`.
- With `V`, the reading starts when the playhead reaches the block.
- At 0, everything starts at the block, as before.
- Record mode keeps its own lead-in.

## New: Esc takes you back to the timeline

- Press `Esc` anywhere, and the keys work on the timeline again.
- It leaves sliders, menus and boxes, such as the mix slider or a block's volume.
- If a block is open, `Esc` closes it from any of its fields.
- Dialogs, header menus, Comments and the shortcuts list go back to the timeline too.
- If you opened a dialog while typing in a block, `Esc` takes you back to your typing.
- While recording, `Esc` discards the take from anywhere, even from a box.

## Fixed: dialogs that ignored Esc

- Some dialogs, such as Diagnostics, now close with `Esc`.

## New: spelling and grammar check

- Exporting now checks the script first, and lists anything that looks wrong.
- Click a suggestion to fix it, or choose **Export anyway**. You can always export.
- To check without exporting, press `Alt+Shift+K`, or choose **Export → Check spelling and grammar**.
- **Add to project** saves names, so they aren't flagged again.
- It works offline, for American, British or Canadian spelling. It only checks English.
- Turn it off, or change the spelling, in Settings under General.

## New: Check grammar with AI

- This button in the check finds harder mistakes, using your AI provider.
- It sends the whole script, so an online provider may charge for it.
- Nothing changes until you choose a fix.

## New: smaller QC packages

- Packages no longer hold audio for Piper blocks, so they stay small.
- The reviewer's computer reads those blocks live, and changed Piper blocks can be heard straight away.
- If a reviewer doesn't have a package's Piper voice, Scribecue offers to download it.
- Google Cloud and Kokoro blocks still keep their audio in the package.
- Writers and reviewers both need 0.83 or later.

## Fixed: videos no browser can open

- TS, M2TS, AVI, WMV and MPG files no longer tell you to try Chrome or Edge, which wouldn't help.
- The message now asks for an MP4 or WebM copy.
- The Getting Started guide shows how to make an MP4 copy.

## New: comments in Write

- You can now leave comments in Write mode, not just QC.
- You don't need a QC package to leave notes on your own script.
- Click **Comment** in an open block, click **Comments** at the top, or right-click the timeline.
- Comments with no name now say **No name** instead of **Reviewer**.

## Changed: the Export menu

- Export is now grouped by who each file is for, such as **For a reviewer** or **For a narrator**.
- **Narration package** is now called **Narration zip**. It holds the same files.

## Fixed: changing audio tracks

- After changing tracks, the old track's sound no longer plays under the new waveform.
- The first time you use a track, the video goes silent until **Getting the sound ready** finishes.
- This wait is much shorter than before on long films.
- Going back to a track you've already used is instant.

## Fixed: several audio tracks in Firefox

- A second audio track no longer stutters, cuts out or shifts in pitch.

## New: AC-3 and E-AC-3 videos have sound

- These videos used to open silent, with no waveform. Now they play.
- The first time you open one, the sound takes a moment. **Getting the sound ready** shows over the video.
- The sound for the last three videos is kept, so they open straight away.
- The waveform, speech to text and the full mix work with these videos too.

## Changed

- DTS and TrueHD videos still can't play in most browsers. Scribecue now says so when you open one.

## New: find and fill the gaps faster

- `D` and `Shift+D` now stop only at free gaps, and skip gaps you've already filled.
- Press `Shift+N`, or double-click a gap on the dialogue lane, to fill it with a new block.

## New: see blocks that run over dialogue

- A block over dialogue has a yellow line on the timeline. The list and editor say so too.
- With text to speech on, this goes by the reading.
- Press `U` or `Shift+U` to jump between these blocks.
- It's a hint, not an error: subtitles can stay up after the words end, so check by ear.

## New: see the dialogue on the timeline

- If a video has subtitles, a dialogue lane shows under the blocks, with the length of each gap.
- Press `D` or `Shift+D` to jump to the next or previous gap.
- Use **Dialogue** under the video to pick other subtitles or turn the lane off.
- No subtitles in the video? Pick **Load a subtitle file…** to use an SRT or WebVTT file.
- An MKV's subtitles can take a while the first time. They load while the video is paused, so it plays smoothly.

## Diagnostics

- The report now shows when the picture has frozen.
- It counts only frames really shown.

## Smoother with long scripts

- Typing, choosing blocks, undo and changing modes respond much faster, especially on slower computers.
- **Fit speeds to timings** and **Make all readings** run faster in long scripts.
- Exporting the description track uses less memory.
- In long scripts, the search above the list updates when you pause typing.

## Fixed

- On smaller screens, the Diagnostics window no longer scrolls as a whole. Only the report scrolls, and its buttons stay in view.

## New: Diagnostics, for problem reports

- In **Settings**, **General**, click **Diagnostics…** to see details to send with a problem report: your browser, the video's format, how playback is going and recent errors.
- Click **Copy** or **Save as file**. Nothing is sent by Scribecue.
- File names are left out unless you click **Include file names**.
- Open it straight after a problem happens, before reloading the page.

## Smoother on slower computers

- While a new video's waveform builds, it now waits when you jump and slows down while the video plays. Jumps are faster and playback smoother, especially in long films.
- The waveform finishes at full speed whenever the video is paused.
- The bar under the video and the playhead take less work to draw.

## Jumping in long videos

- When a jump takes a moment, **Seeking…** shows next to the clock until the picture arrives.
- Dragging along the timeline or the bar under the video now shows the picture as you go, instead of only when you let go.

## Fixed

- If Chrome or Edge can't show Scribecue's Open window, the browser's own file window opens instead, so you can still open files.

## Fixed

- **Open** works again in Chrome, Edge and Chromium. Since 0.77.0 it showed an error instead of the file picker.
- **Export → Session package** works again in those browsers.
- Session packages now end in .scribesession. Packages saved by 0.77.0 still open: drag one onto Scribecue, or choose All files in the Open window.

## New: takes in a folder you choose

- When you open a recording file, choose a folder for its takes. Each take is saved there as you record it.
- Firefox and Safari keep takes in the browser instead. In Chrome and Edge, you can choose that too.
- Takes kept in the browser can move to a folder with **Move takes to a folder…**.
- Takes from earlier versions move into the folder when you first open the recording.

## New: session packages

- **Export → Session package** puts the script and your takes in one file, to carry on on another computer.
- Choose every take, or only the takes in the export.
- Open the package in Scribecue on the other computer, and choose a folder for the takes.

## New: recording

- The take you're recording grows on the timeline, with its waveform.
- `Space` stops recording and keeps the take.
- `Esc` stops recording and discards the take. The playhead goes back to where it was.
- Deleted or discarded a take by mistake? Press `Ctrl/Cmd+Z`, or click the message, to bring it back.

## Changed

- A block's slot now ends where the block ends, not a second after.
- First-time setup offers Transcribe, Write and QC. Record mode's setup opens when you open a recording file.
- **Pickups WAV** shows in the Export menu only when the recording file asks for pickups.

## New: notes for the narrator

- Each block has a **Notes** box above its text, for direction or how to say a name.
- Text to speech doesn't read the notes. They don't change the block's timing.
- In Record mode, the narrator sees them with the block.

## New: alts in Record mode

- Press `A`, or switch the open block to **Alt**, to write and record your own wording for it.
- Switch between the original and the alt at any time.
- With alts, **Export → Narration package** gives a zip: the narration WAV, an alts WAV and a notes file.
- When checking the narration, the writer can use an alt's wording. The block keeps its timing.

## New: timeline zoom

- Zoom with −, + and **Fit** at the top right of the timeline. It shows how much is on screen.
- In Record mode, press `Z` or click **Take** to zoom to the selected block's take. Press `Z` again to zoom back.
- Zoomed right in, the waveforms are sharp enough to line up single sounds.

## Changed

- **Return to start** now works only in Record mode, and its setting shows only there.

## Fixed

- Speech to text could hear silence in some audio-only MP4 and M4A files.
- Exporting the narration of a long programme is much faster.

## Fixed

- In QC, the **Comment** button in an open block is now on the right. Its tooltip no longer runs off the edge of the window.

## New: Mic check and the level pocket

- **Mic check**, next to Punch in, opens a tall meter. Read a few lines, including your loudest, and watch where your peaks land.
- Aim for the pocket: −12 to −6 dBFS. Quieter is fine for softer lines. Never go over −6.
- Takes in the pocket now say so. Takes up to −6 count, where before only −12 to −8 did.

## New: setup for each mode

- The first time you use a mode, a short setup for it opens. That includes opening a QC package or a recording file.
- Record mode's setup helps you pick your microphone, test your level and choose a lead-in.

## Changed

- In QC, send your review back with **Export → Return package**. SRT and VTT exports are hidden while a QC package is open.

## New: choose which QC changes to keep

- Returned QC reviews no longer change your script without asking. Each block change goes to a new **Pending review** tab above the script.
- Accept (✓) or reject (✗) each change. The timeline outlines where the reviewer’s version would go.
- Edit the reviewer’s wording, start or end before accepting.
- Comments still come in by themselves.

## Fixes

- Splitting a block keeps its own voice, volume, programme dip and speed in both halves. Before, the second half read in the project’s voice.
- When a subtitle file has a block whose times can’t be read, its Scribecue settings no longer move to the next block.

## Fixes

- Blocks read by Google, Piper or Kokoro voices now end where the voice stops, not after the silence at the end of each reading. Google adds up to half a second or more.
- Blocks that follow their reading get a little shorter the first time you open a project.
- In QC, new readings in older packages are measured the same way when you open them.

## Fixes

- In QC, an edited block now ends where its new reading finishes, up to the start of the next block.
- Blocks saved running past their new reading are fixed when you open the package.
- If a new reading runs into the next block, a message says the end stops there.

## Fixes

- In QC, an edited block now always ends where its reading finishes, even if you change the words back. Before, the reading could run past the end.
- In the TTS preview, an edited block heard in its own voice follows its reading too.

## Fixes

- **Return to start** now puts the playhead back as soon as you stop, so play starts right where it sits. Before, it jumped back when you pressed play.
- If Scribecue can’t read a script you open, it now says why, rather than doing nothing.

## Voices from Frazier scripts

- Opening an `.adc` script that names voices now asks whether to use them.
- Choose other voices to pick one in place of each: one for the project, and one for each set of blocks with their own voice.
- It only asks while text to speech is on.

## New Google readings in QC

- In an editable QC package with Google voices, a changed block is read when you finish editing it, as in Write mode. Its end moves to fit the new reading.
- Blocks you add in QC are read too, with the package’s Google voice.
- Your own Google key is used first. If it fails, or you don’t have one, the writer’s key in the package is used.
- **Hear rewrite** is gone. Press V to hear a block.
- QC packages with readings for added blocks need this version or later to open.

## Clearer voice changes in QC

- In an editable QC package, a block changed to another voice now says **New voice · needs a fresh package**.
- Hover over it to see why: a different voice can’t make new audio in QC. Ask the writer for a fresh package, or change the voice back.

## Return to start

- Turn on **Return to start** under **Settings → General**. Play after a stop then goes back to where you last started playing, to hear a part again.
- Move the playhead while stopped to start somewhere else.
- It's off at first. `RETURN` shows under the video while it's on.

## Bring back sound you cut from a take

- In Record mode, drag the end of a take's part back out to bring back sound you trimmed, split off or deleted.
- It stops at the next part, or at the start or end of the recording.
- In **Fine-tune**, a trim below 0 does the same.

## Your name on comments

- Add your name under **Settings → General**, or in setup's QC step. It fills in your name on comments.
- It's optional. A name typed only in the Comments drawer is no longer saved.

## Bring QC feedback back into your project

- Open **QC → Compare returned review** to combine a reviewer’s findings with your work. Independent changes combine; conflicting block corrections need your choice.
- **Accept review** keeps your authoring project editable in QC and Write, with the original recordings available for comparison.
- Use **Locate original readings** to restore the matching audio on another computer.

## Hear Google rewrites

- Editable QC packages can include a separate Google review key. Your main key is never filled in.
- **Hear rewrite** reads changed wording or speed with the original Google voice and saves the recording for replay. Moving a block reuses saved audio.
- The reviewer’s own key is used first. If it fails, Scribecue offers to retry that reading with the bundled key.
- **Save** keeps the review key for continued work. **Save return package** leaves it out. New readings need internet; saved recordings play offline.

## Pickups

- In Write mode, click **Pickup** on a block to ask the narrator to record it again. Add a note, such as how to say a name.
- Each recording file you export is a new version. It asks for the blocks you marked and the lines you reworded.
- Takes carry over to the new version, so the narrator records only the pickups.
- In Record mode, P goes to the next pickup. **Compare** plays the original take, then the pickup.
- **Export → Pickups WAV** holds only the new takes, each where it belongs. Its markers carry your notes.
- Opening a returned WAV shows which pickups are recorded, and can clear their marks.
- Started recording before 0.68.0? Open the new recording file, then bring in the earlier takes under **Microphone, lead-in and sync**.

## Fine-tune a take

- In Record mode, a take’s **Edit** button is now called **Fine-tune**. It moves, trims or splits the take by the millisecond, and works from the keyboard.
- It shows only on the take in the export, as the timeline does.

## Takes on the timeline

- In Record mode, each block’s picked take shows as a clip on the timeline, under the video’s waveform.
- Drag a clip to move it, or drag its ends to trim it. Double-click to play it.
- Right-click a clip to trim silence, start it at the block, fit it in its slot, or reset it.
- X splits the selected block’s take at the playhead. You no longer need to open Edit first.
- Each block’s slot is shaded green, and any part of a take past it shows in red.

## Fixed

- The selected block no longer disappears from the list when Record mode opens.

## Help

- New troubleshooting guide, and screenshots in the recording guide.

## Hear the Kokoro voices

- The voices guide has samples of four Kokoro voices: Heart, Liam, Alice and Lewis. Click a name to hear it.
- All the voice samples now play at the same volume, so they’re easier to compare.

## Fixed

- Piper voice samples in the voices guide now play in every browser when you run Scribecue in Docker. Before, some browsers wouldn’t play them.

## Hear the Piper voices

- The voices guide has a short sample of each Piper voice. Click a name to hear it before you download it.
- Samples play inside the guide window. Click the name again to stop.

## Start fresh after QC

- **New** is available while reviewing a QC package. Start a blank project in Write mode without opening another file first.
- Unsaved reviews offer **Save and start new project**, **Start without saving**, or **Cancel**. A cancelled or failed save keeps your review open.
- Starting fresh closes the review and video, and clears the package’s restrictions and undo history. Reopen your saved package to return to the review.

## QC editing permissions

- Choose **Allow reviewers to edit blocks** when creating a QC package. It starts off for comments-only reviews.
- QC shows whether edits are allowed. Reviewers can’t change this choice, and it stays with the package when saving or recovering a review.
- Comments-only packages stay in QC. Packages from before this change also open as comments only.
- Update Scribecue before opening a new QC package.

## QC review

- Choose **QC** to listen and leave comments. Comments and block Comment buttons now appear only in this mode.
- **Allow edits** lets you correct blocks while keeping Comments open. It starts off, and timings never adjust automatically in QC.
- Block comments target the open block. The Comments button targets the playhead; right-click the timeline to choose another time.

## Original readings on another computer

- **Export → QC package** includes the project and its original TTS readings. Send the matching video separately. Reviewers need no matching voices or keys.
- Package Piper, Kokoro or Google Cloud readings. Built-in and browser-provided voices need a recorded review mix instead.
- Missing voices open a project in QC with saved timings preserved. An approximate TTS preview must be chosen explicitly.
- Moving or resizing a block keeps its audio and flags overruns. Text, pronunciation, voice or speed changes mark the reading out of date. **Hear previous reading** plays the old clip alone.

## Guide

- The [QC guide](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/Guides/QC.md) covers preparing a handoff, listening, comments, corrections and returning the review.

## Comments for QC

- Click **Comment** in an open block to add a comment to it. Add as many as you need.
- Open **Comments** at the top, or press **Alt+Shift+C**, to see the project's comments. Choose **Timeline time**, or right-click the timeline, to comment at a fixed time.
- Add your name if you like. Edit, delete, resolve or reopen comments, and click a block or time to jump there.
- Comments stay in the `.scribecue` project. Save it to hand over for review; the reviewer saves a copy to send back.

## Voices

- On a Mac, the voice list no longer shows some voices twice, such as Samantha in Chrome.
- Voice names no longer repeat their language, as in “Eddy (English (United Kingdom)) (en-GB)”. They now read “Eddy (en-GB)”.
- The voices guide says that browsers can’t use the Mac’s Enhanced and Premium voices. For a natural voice, use Piper or Kokoro.

## Guides

- The guides now live in a **Guides** folder on GitHub. The README stays where it was.
- Links to the guides in Scribecue, and in What’s new, point to their new place on GitHub.

## Fixing a late start

- **Start at block** in a take’s editor moves the take so its sound starts where the block does.
- Dragged edges now snap to the block’s start and end, the playhead and the take’s other parts.
- So a late start takes two steps: trim the start up to the playhead, then click **Start at block**.

## Guides

- The recording guide now lists Firefox for recording, alongside Chrome, Edge and Safari.

## Record mode for narrators

- In Write mode, **Export → Recording file** saves your script for a narrator. They can’t change it.
- The narrator opens it with the video and records each block, with a lead-in and a level meter.
- Every take is kept. While the video plays, you hear the take picked for each block. **TAKES** under the video turns that off.
- **Export → Narration WAV** gives the mixer one timestamped file, with a marker at each block.
- Open the narration WAV with your script to check the narrator’s copy wasn’t changed.

## Fixing takes

- **Punch in** (Shift+Enter) picks up a take from the playhead and keeps what came before.
- **Edit** shows a take over its block’s slot. Drag to move it or trim its ends.
- **Split** (X) cuts a take at the playhead. Move the parts closer, or delete one (Delete).
- **Trim silence** and **Fit in slot** do the common fixes in one click. **Reset** undoes them all.

## Keeping takes

- Takes are kept in your browser. In Docker, the takes container keeps them on disk instead.
- **Settings → Offline and storage** shows how much space takes use, with **Delete all**.

The [recording guide](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/Guides/RECORDING.md) has the details.

## Fixes

- When a browser doesn’t give its name, the notice about missing features now says **This browser is missing some features**, instead of “You’re using this browser”.
- If you close Scribecue while ffmpeg is making a copy or a full mix, its files in Docker are now deleted after five minutes, instead of waiting for the next job.

## When a video won’t play

- Some Chromium builds can’t play H.264 video or AAC sound, which most MP4 files use. Scribecue now tells you when it starts.
- Opening a file it can’t play names what’s missing and what to do, instead of a short message.
- With ffmpeg in Docker, **Make a copy that plays** makes a copy, opens it and downloads it for you. When only the sound is the problem, the picture is kept as it is.

## Guides

- The guides now say what your computer needs to run Scribecue, and how much memory Docker needs for each voice.

## Projects sound the same everywhere

- A project now keeps the settings that block dips and volumes build on: whether the video’s sound goes down under readings, how far, how quickly, and the **Video / TTS** slider.
- Opening the project puts them back, so it sounds the same on another computer.
- Projects saved before this leave your settings as they are.

## Volume for each block

- The open block has a **Vol** slider, from 25% to 200%, to make its reading quieter or louder than the rest. Type an exact percentage in the box beside it and press Enter, or double-click the slider for 100%.
- It works with the **Video / TTS** slider: move that, and every block moves with it, keeping its difference.
- It’s used while playing, in the full mix and in the description track, and kept in projects and WebVTT exports.
- Readings are already close to full volume, so above 100% they sound fuller more than louder, and are kept from distorting. The browser’s own voices go no louder than 100%.

## Dips that follow the setting

- A block’s dip is now more or less than the one in the text to speech settings: **5 dB more**, **10 dB more**, **5 dB less**, or **Custom** to type any amount, such as +7 or -3. **No dip** is still there.
- Change the setting later, and every block’s dip moves with it.
- Blocks given an exact dip in 0.59 or 0.60 sound the same as before: they become the difference from your setting.

## Fixes

- A block’s own dip is no longer lost when the page is reloaded.

## Custom dips

- **Lower it by**, in the text to speech settings, has a new **Custom** choice: type any amount from 1 to 40 dB, for when 6, 10, 15 or 20 dB isn’t quite right.
- A block’s dip menu has **Custom** too: type 0 to 40 dB, then press Enter. Escape leaves it as it was.
- Custom dips work everywhere the others do: while playing, in the full mix, and in projects and WebVTT exports.
- A block’s own dip replaces the setting for that block; the two never add up.

## Export a full mix

- **Export → Full mix** saves the programme and the readings together in one stereo file, as it sounds when you play: the programme goes down under each reading, and the levels follow the **Video / TTS** slider.
- Save it as a WAV, or as an MP3 to keep it small. The description track can be saved as an MP3 too.
- **Loudness:** bring the mix to −23 LUFS (EBU R 128), −24 LUFS (ATSC A/85), −16 LUFS for podcasts or −14 LUFS for streaming. Peaks are kept from clipping.
- **Stems:** also save the lowered programme and the readings as separate files, to mix again in your editor.
- Long films are mixed a piece at a time, so a two-hour film doesn’t have to fit in memory, and Scribecue stays responsive while it works.

## Put it in the video

- If ffmpeg is installed on your computer, Scribecue shows the commands, ready to copy, that put the mix into the video, as an extra audio description track or in place of its sound.
- Running Scribecue yourself? Add the new ffmpeg container, and it does this for you, and can also save the mix as AAC, AC-3 or E-AC-3. See “The full mix in the video” in the install guide.

## How far the programme goes down

- In the text to speech settings, choose how far the programme goes down under readings (6 to 20 dB) and how quickly.
- Each block can have its own, from the new menu next to its speed in the editor: for example **No dip** for a quiet scene, or **Dip 20 dB** under loud music. It’s saved with the project and in WebVTT.

## Smoother on slower computers

- Long jobs, such as **Make all readings** or **Fit speeds to timings** on a long script, no longer make Scribecue stutter or freeze while they run, and finish sooner.
- **Loading…** shows next to the clock while the video gets ready to play, so play no longer looks as if it did nothing.
- Pressing play and pause quickly no longer shows a “Playback failed” message.
- Getting started has tips for slower computers, such as writing with a smaller copy of the video.

## Fixes

- **Fit speeds to timings** no longer gives up on a block whose reading is still too long at the slowest speed: it tries faster ones until the reading fits.

## Waveforms are kept

- Reopening a video, even after a reload, shows its waveform straight away, instead of building it again.
- Waveforms are kept in your browser for the 20 videos and audio tracks used most recently, and take little space: about 3 MB for a two-hour film.
- In a file with several audio tracks, the waveform shows straight away, while Scribecue still copies the track out to play it.
- **Remove all data**, in **Settings**, clears them too.

## Guides

- The AI help guide now recommends OpenAI models: GPT-6.1 Sol to start with, GPT-6 Astra for busy or tricky scenes, and GPT-6 Luna for cheap first drafts, with roughly what each costs per draft.

## Fixes

- After **Fit speeds to timings**, blocks that fit no longer stay red in the list until they’re read. It happened most with a base speed other than 100%, when some blocks were left at a speed that hadn’t been read, so their lengths were only estimates.

## Fixes

- Playing without a video, readings now start and end with their blocks. In Firefox especially, they used to start a little late, most of all when you pressed play right at a block.

## Run it on your computer

- In the web version, a short message after the tour and setup says you can also run Scribecue on your own computer with Docker, for Kokoro voices and more. It only shows once.
- **Run it on your computer**, in **Settings** under **General**, opens the guide any time.

## Simpler guides

- The guides are split into shorter ones: Getting started, Writing, Voices, Transcribing, AI help, Shortcuts, Google voices and Running it yourself. Each has its own tab under **Guides** in the shortcuts overlay (**?**).
- They’re rewritten to be quicker to read, with keys in tables and out-of-date parts fixed.

## Fixes

## Opening and closing blocks

- As in Frazier, the selected block now opens right where it is in the list, instead of in a box above it. Every other block shows its start and end, with its text underneath.

- **Frame** steps move exactly one frame of the video.

## Swap sides

- A new **⇄** button at the start of the top bar puts the video on the left and the editor and block list on the right. Click it again to put them back. Scribecue remembers which you chose.

## Blocks end where their reading ends

- In Write mode with text to speech on, every block now ends where its reading ends, as in Frazier. To make a block longer or shorter, change its speed, from its menu or with **[** and **]**.
- A block’s edges can no longer be dragged, and OUT shows where the reading ends. Dragging a block, or changing its IN, moves the whole block. Splitting and merging keep each end at its reading.
- Blocks opened from a file keep their timing until you edit them.
- The settings **Set the end of new blocks from the reading** and **Change a block’s reading speed when you resize it** are gone, since this always happens now.
- In Transcribe mode, and with text to speech off, edges drag as before.

## Natural speeds

- **Fit speeds to timings** never slows a reading below −15%, so a short line in a long block still sounds natural, with silence after it.

## Try voices before switching

- Picking a voice in the text to speech settings, from the list or your favourites, now only tries it out. **Test** reads with it, and nothing else changes, so you can go through voices without being asked about the timings each time.
- When you’ve found the one you want, click **Apply**, next to Test. Every block then reads with it, and you’re asked about the timings once. Close Settings without Apply and the voice stays as it was.

## Your own test line

- A new **Test text** box under the voice holds what Test reads. It starts with the sample description; type any line to hear it in each voice. It’s remembered for next time.

## Fixes

- Every block now fits its reading as you edit it. Blocks marked with H, drawn on the timeline or opened from a file keep their length, and their reading speeds up or slows down to fill it. A block with a speed you picked keeps that speed, and its end moves to where the reading finishes. Before, these blocks kept both their length and their speed, so a longer line ran past the end of its block.

## Fixes

- After **Shift+V** or **Update all timings** set a block’s end from its reading, the end now keeps following the reading as you edit the text, as a new block’s does. Before, it stayed where it was, so a longer line, or a Google reading that came out longer than its estimate, left the block too short, marked ⚠, with its reading running past the end. This also applies when you open a script and choose to change the ends to match the readings.

## Fixes

- Resizing a block now settles on a reading speed that fills it in a reading or two. Before, with Kokoro voices especially, the speed could wander for a few seconds, through speeds whose readings ran past the block’s end, and stop somewhere slightly off.
- Resizing a block whose speed you picked by hand now says that it keeps that speed, and how to have the reading fill the block instead.

## A voice for each block

- The block editor has a new **Voice** menu next to the speed. Leave it on **Same as Settings** to use the voice chosen in Settings, or pick another voice for just that block, for example a different voice for subtitles or a second narrator.
- Blocks with their own voice show its name in the list. Playing, fitting, Make all readings and exported description tracks all use each block’s own voice, and a track can mix Piper, Kokoro and Google voices.
- Block voices are saved in projects and WebVTT exports. Frazier `.adc` files bring their per-block voices with them.
- If a block’s voice isn’t available, for example a Kokoro voice in the web version, it reads with the voice in Settings until it is.

## Replace all voices

- When blocks have voices of their own, the text to speech settings say which, with a **Replace all voices** button that sets every block back to the voice chosen there. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes it.

## Steadier fitting

- Fitting a block’s speed now settles on the reading that fills the block best without running over. Before, it could stop on a speed that came out slightly short or a little long, especially with Kokoro voices.

## Make all readings

- A new **Make all readings** button in the text to speech settings reads every block now, at its own speed, without changing any timings. Each block then plays straight away and its length is exact.
- The readings are kept in your browser, so they're still ready after a reload or the next time you open the project, and they work offline.
- It runs in the background, with its progress and a Stop button in the bottom bar. Blocks already read are skipped.

## Readings kept across reloads

- Piper and Kokoro readings are now kept in your browser, as Google's already were. After you reload or reopen Scribecue, blocks already read keep their ● dot and exact length, and play straight away, even offline.
- Up to 250 MB of readings are kept. When that fills up, Piper and Kokoro readings go first, since they're free to make again, then the ones used longest ago. Settings, under Storage, shows them as Saved readings and can clear them.

## Readings on time while playing

- While playing, Scribecue now makes the next blocks' readings ahead of the playhead. Before, a reading was only made as its block began, so Kokoro voices, which take a second or more, started late and ran past the end of their block. Exported description tracks were never affected.

Since 0.48.0, Scribecue couldn't see them: the Natural voices section was hidden, and voices you'd downloaded were missing from the voice list, so blocks were read with a browser voice instead. Your downloaded voices were kept, so they're there again without downloading them.

## New: Piper voices, exact timings and description track export

Scribecue can now use [Piper](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl), an open-source speech engine with natural-sounding voices, running in a second container next to the editor. Its voices run on your computer and work offline, so your script never leaves it. Piper is optional: Scribecue works as before without it.

With a Piper voice, in Write mode:

- **Lengths are exact straight away.** A block's reading time is exact as soon as it has text, and **Update all timings** uses the real readings in a second or two, with no silent read-through.
- **Each line always takes the same time,** so the timing you see is the timing you get, between sessions and in the export.
- **Export description track** saves every block's reading as one WAV file, each starting at its block's start time and as long as the video, ready to mix with the programme. It tells you if any readings overlap.

Four English voices are included: Lessac and Ryan (US), and Alba and Alan (UK). You can choose others from the Piper voice list.

### Setting it up

Create a file called `.env` in the Scribecue folder containing `COMPOSE_PROFILES=piper`, then run `docker compose up -d --build`. The first build downloads Piper and its voices, about 1 GB. After that the Piper container has no internet access, and only Scribecue's own server can reach it. See the README for details.
